headline: 1Password says it will publish a root cause analysis in the coming weeks; no organisation that uses it has said it was affected.
summary: Re-read 1Password's incident post (s001): it now opens with a promise of a root cause analysis 'in the coming weeks once our full investigation is complete' (new claim c013, Confirmed, the company's own post); the rest of the post is unchanged. TechCrunch (s002) and BleepingComputer (s003) are unchanged and still had no reply from 1Password. New question q010, which organisations use 1Password and were they affected: 1Password's own customer pages name Canva, Asana, DigitalOcean, JetBrains and Elastic (s005 to s009, claims c014 to c018, Reported; use is not impact), and no organisation has said it was affected (c019, Not established). Where we looked: 1Password's post and customer pages, SEC 8-K filings naming 1Password since Nov 15 (none about this), and The Verge, Help Net Security and SecurityWeek, which retell the post and name no customer. Nothing on how many customers (q004), how the account was taken over (q005), who did it (q006) or how the code was deployed (q008); no regulator notice found. Theory sweep: Hacker News thread 50644817 (708 comments) and 50649132 (3) read; commenters keep raising missing code review (q008), a stolen token or laptop as the way in (c003), tampered apps (q007) and phishing from the copied emails (c008), all already covered; Reddit refused automated reading. Main answer, answer_group and size unchanged; size_basis now says whether customers' organisations were affected is not known. Not eligible for resolved: a root cause analysis is still promised.
author: Research agent

headline: 1Password says its apps and browser extensions were untouched; how the attacker's code reached its servers is still unexplained.
summary: Re-read 1Password's incident post and TechCrunch, and read BleepingComputer (s003, Tier 2) and the Hacker News discussion of the post (s004, Tier 5, read for the questions people are raising, not as evidence). New claims: c009 (Reported) apps and browser extensions not affected, 1Password's word alone; c010 (Not established) how the code was deployed; c011 (Confirmed) private source code copied and build system reached, from 1Password's own post; c012 (Reported) copied invitation and recovery tokens cannot be used alone. c003 now notes 1Password's reference to a stolen token and the guesses about a hacked laptop; c007 notes that BleepingComputer had no reply. New rumors q007 (apps tampered with: Reported, 1Password says no) and q008 (no code review: Not established), and question q009 (recovery links). Added what the subject is, one known item and one not-known item. Main answer, answer_group and size unchanged. No attribution theory and no claim of responsibility found; no statement from 1Password beyond its post; neither outlet had a reply. Privacy check done: no commenters, reporters or staff named.
author: Research agent

headline: 1Password's logo now leads this page; no finding changed.
summary: Picture only: Wikimedia Commons has no photograph of 1Password, so its logo, from 1Password's own newsroom, is shown whole on a plain background and captioned as used for identification. No claim, label, source or question changed, and this is not a check of the story.

headline: 1Password says an attacker copied some customers' names, emails and account details from its backend; it says vaults were not affected.
summary: New incident page. Read 1Password's incident post (Nov 25) and TechCrunch (Nov 25). Main answer Confirmed and answer_group hack-stated: 1Password itself says an attacker gained access to backend systems. incident_type breach: customer account data was copied. No service: 1Password says its apps and services are working normally, and nothing is reported down. The vault claim is the company's word alone, so Reported. Open: how many customers, how the GitHub account was taken over, who did it. Privacy check done: no people named; the support address in the post is left out.
author: Research agent
